summary: The note examines how local media coverage shaped the municipal elections held on October 15, 2023, through informing voters, endorsements, agenda-setting, investigative watchdog reporting, social media, ownership bias, and voter turnout. It illustrates each mechanism with examples from towns such as Fairview, Riverdale, Westbrook, Eastwood, Mountain Valley and Brookhaven. It concludes that local media is powerful and needs scrutiny, and recommends media literacy, diverse ownership and journalistic integrity.
one_line: Local media coverage influenced the October 15, 2023 municipal elections via information, endorsements, agenda-setting, accountability, social media, bias and turnout.
key_facts: The recent municipal elections were held on October 15, 2023.
Voter turnout is typically lower in municipal elections than in federal or state elections, and analysts correlate variations with the intensity and nature of local media coverage.
In Fairview, journalist Rebecca Torres of the "Fairview Gazette" profiled each council candidate with interviews and policy breakdowns, which appeared to correlate with an informed voter base.
The "Metro City Times" endorsement of mayoral candidate James O'Connor was seen as a pivotal factor in his narrow win over incumbent Mayor Lisa Franklin.
In Riverdale, the "Riverdale Reporter" published exposés on the water quality crisis, which came to dominate forum discussions and pushed candidates to pledge resolutions.
In Westbrook, columnist Michael Evans of "Westbrook Weekly" uncovered past financial mismanagement by council candidate Deborah Liu, who then lost to Steven Kim.
In Eastwood, mayoral hopeful Andrea Vasquez used Instagram stories and live streams, reportedly improving her share of the vote among younger voters.
The "Hometown Herald", owned by business tycoon Richard Hall, was accused of biased coverage favoring Hall's preferred candidates in Mountain Valley.
Brookhaven, where local media gave robust electoral coverage, reported higher voter participation, while areas with scant coverage saw apathy and lower turnout.
Key issues in the 2023 elections included property tax revisions, public safety, infrastructural development and sustainability initiatives.
The note recommends bolstering public media literacy, ensuring diverse media ownership, and fostering journalistic integrity.
